claims.text: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi surveyed 1,252 paying guest accommodation buildings between September 7 and 9 following the Satya Niketan building collapse.
Out of 1,252 surveyed PG buildings, 1,201 were found visibly safe, 39 required minor repairs, 9 required major repairs, and 3 were declared dangerous.
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi identified 26 framed structures above G+4 floors for close monitoring due to structural vulnerability.
Between June 1 and September 3, 2026, the MCD carried out demolitions at 983 properties, sealed 464 properties, and issued 1,516 show-cause notices for unauthorised construction in Delhi.
Renovation work conducted around 10 days before the collapse involved filling approximately three truckloads of construction debris into the basement of the Satya Niketan building.
On the day of the collapse, a wall on the ground floor of the Satya Niketan building was removed to create additional space for a shop.
Seven people were killed when the five-storey building in Satya Niketan collapsed on September 6.
Police apprehended and arrested 35-year-old labour contractor Sanoj Kumar from Kasganj in Uttar Pradesh for supervising the renovation work.
Paying guest operator Shudhanshu Lovneesh and associate Shubham Tyagi leased four floors of the Satya Niketan building in August 2025 for Rs 1.05 lakh per month.
Following the building collapse, local journalists and student activists reported severe mobile internet slowdowns in Satya Niketan and alleged the government had used jammers.
Delhi Police issued a social media statement denying internet slowdown allegations, stating that networks were fully operational in Satya Niketan.
The Telecommunications Rules notified by the Indian government in November 2024 empower officials to suspend telecommunication services for up to 15 days.
Delhi Police arrested Sudhanshu, operator of the 'Hostel Daze' PG facility housed inside the collapsed Satya Niketan building, while co-operator Shubham Tyagi remained on the run.
Property owners Hariram Bansal, aged 81, and Urmila Gupta, aged 75, were sent to 14 days of judicial custody following the building collapse.
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta ordered the Municipal Corporation of Delhi to demolish the dilapidated building adjoining the collapse site.
A Supreme Court bench comprising Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R Mahadevan agreed to examine regulatory compliance regarding illegal PG structures on a pan-India basis.
India is hosting the 18th BRICS Summit on September 12-13, 2026, at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will host a gala dinner for leaders participating in the BRICS Summit on Saturday evening.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to hold a formal bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Saturday during the BRICS Summit.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to hold a bilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday.
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal will meet Russian counterpart Anton Alikhanov at INNOPROM India 2026 in New Delhi on Thursday.
India and Russia have set a bilateral trade target of $100 billion, or approximately Rs 9.45 lakh crore, by 2030.
The INNOPROM India 2026 industrial trade fair takes place at Bharat Mandapam from September 9 to 11.
The National Industrial Corridor Development Programme spans 11 industrial corridors and 20 greenfield industrial smart cities across 13 Indian states.
The official theme for the 2026 BRICS Summit in New Delhi is 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'.
BRICS originated as the BRIC alliance between Brazil, Russia, India, and China in 2006, held its first summit in Yekaterinburg in 2009, and admitted South Africa in 2011.
BRICS expanded to 11 full member states after admitting Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE in January 2024, followed by Indonesia in January 2025.
Delhi Traffic Police issued a public advisory establishing 22 diversion points and regulating traffic across more than 35 roads for the BRICS summit.
Roadside parking within 200 metres of controlled roads during the BRICS summit period is strictly prohibited in Delhi.
Delhi Metro operations will remain fully functional across all stations without disruption during the summit.
Delhi International Airport Ltd operationalised Pier C at Terminal 3 starting September 9 night to manage increased international flight operations during the summit.
Delhi International Airport Ltd set up dedicated immigration counters and special landing and parking arrangements for BRICS summit participants.
